assumptions.description: Task-mandated eight female-by-age-band cells of375; integer uniform ages within bands is author assumption; no participant input and equal-cell mass.
No Mexico source. Cross-population use is uncalibrated transport; no causal or individual-recovery interpretation. Different original populations are not pooled as independent parameter replicates.

Condition on task eligibility rather than simulate undocumented selection. No additional medication/anemia exclusion. S1 plasma,FPG<126;S2 broad/nonuniversal fasting;S3 age30-64,HbA1c<6.5,fast4-17h;S4 age18-75,known diabetes present differ.

Target serum glucose mg/dL. Plasma-to-serum and unspecified Kerman matrix/calibration equivalence assumed; no empirical correction. mmol/L difference converted with18.0182, not feedback identity conversion.
BMI beta support15-45, mean28.01 SD3.8, independent age/sex; mean and SD transferred from different populations; bounds/shape/independence unsupported.
Scaled-beta glucose support50-126 with linear conditional mean and constant conditional variance; lower50 and family assumed; strict upper126 required by task.
Gamma HbA1c with linear conditional mean and constant conditional variance, no upper6.5 exclusion; family and lack of interactions assumed.

Use (q97.5-mean)/Phi^-1(.975) from NHANES50-54 as a working age/sex-residual HbA1c SD. Normal-location approximation, use as conditional scale and gamma transfer are assumptions; it is not reported SD.
Transfer Kerman marginal BMI SD3.8 and glucose SD12.4 to age/sex residual scales; data do not identify these conditional scales.

Finnish R-squared and margins are survey-weighted and use BINARY age30-44 vs45-64, plus fasting time for glucose. Nested common-sample projection interpretation and transfer to CONTINUOUS-age adjustment at fixed fasting context are assumptions; positive roots/signs assumed.
Use Kerman raw Pearson0.23 as age/sex-residual correlation by assumption. It remains raw Pearson in feedback; no substitution with partial/weighted/Spearman.

Combine residual magnitudes/scales from different cohorts into one positive-definite working covariance; no common cohort identifies it and no statistical probability for transport uncertainty is claimed.
Negate Taiwan male0.08301 coefficient adjusted age only, then treat as fully adjusted female contrast. Finnish weighted female-minus-male glucose margin transported as conditional contrast.
Transfer NHANES age-HbA1c0.010/year conditional slope; glucose8mg/dL contrast over an assumed40year span gives0.2/year. Anchor age52 for50-54 row is an assumption.
Center at NHANES BMI28.01,female.52,HbA1c5.40,age52; glucose at Kerman91.2,age43.8,female296/525; glucose Hb anchor derived at NHANES centers. Centers are not an empirical common population.

Feedback compares the existing target design output in source-compatible observed age/glucose ranges, not a reconstructed source population; source-selection, age/sex distribution, assays and diagnosis differ. Raw discrepancy is not significance, transport validation or a calibration objective.
Kerman table SD is interpreted as ordinary sample SD(ddof1) for approximate feedback; denominator unreported. No SE or sample size conversion is made.
Only machine-rounded support endpoints are moved to nearest interior float; underflowed HbA1c zero moves to least positive float. No statistical resampling/clipping to tune results.
Deterministic unique identifiers and output ordering carry no scientific relationship.

design.derivation: Task n3000/exact375 in eight cells; uniform integer ages within each cell chosen.

glucose.derivation: age slope8/40;female slope(4.9-5.2)*18.0182;bmi slope=rBG*12.4/3.8;variance=12.4^2*(1-rBG^2);mean affine as proposal.

residual_moments.derivation: sH=(6-5.4)/Phi^-1(.975);rBG=positive sqrt((.1642-.1174)/(1-.1174));rBH=positive sqrt((.1164-.0660)/(1-.0660));rGH=.23 assumed residual;unit factor18.0182 declared.

output.derivation: Task column order and unique sequential row identifiers, no row selection.
